grammar.karakaSummary: bhagavān devaḥ is kartṛ of āyayau; antardhim is its goal-object. surāḥ is kartṛ of jagmuḥ; tad vākyam is karman of ākarṇya; abhimatām diśam is directional karman.
grammar.verbalModality: uktvā and ākarṇya are prior-action absolutives; āyayau and jagmuḥ are perfects.
grammar.sandhi: iti + uktvā → ityuktvā; bhagavān + devaḥ → bhagavāndevaḥ; tatra + eva + antardhim + āyayau → tatraivāntardhimāyayau; surāḥ + tu + ākarṇya → surāstvākarṇya; jagmuḥ + ca + abhimatām → jagmuścābhimatām.

words.karaka: prior action of the blessed god

words.morph: accusative singular feminine past participial adjective

units.speaker: narrator
units.devanagari:
चक्रुर्दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषं प्रलयाभ्ररवोपमम् |
अथ दैत्यैर्महाव्योम्नि तैः पातालतलोत्थितैः ||
units.iast:
cakrurdundubhinirghoṣaṃ pralayābhraravopamam |
atha daityairmahāvyomni taiḥ pātālatalotthitaiḥ ||
units.english: {0:They made} {1:a kettledrum roar} {2:like the roar of a cloud at dissolution}. {3:Then}, {5:in the vast sky}, {4,6:by those demons} {7:risen from the floor of the underworld}—
units.sense: They made a kettledrum roar like the roar of a cloud at dissolution. Then, in the vast sky, by those demons risen from the floor of the underworld—

grammar.karakaSummary: The gods remain the implicit kartṛ of cakruḥ; dundubhi-nirghoṣam is karman and pralaya-abhra-rava-upamam qualifies it. The second half continues syntactically into verse 70: taiḥ daityaiḥ ... utthitaiḥ is instrumental plural and mahā-vyomni locative.
grammar.verbalModality: cakruḥ is perfect third plural; the second half deliberately has no finite verb until avartata in 70.
grammar.sandhi: cakruḥ + dundubhi → cakrurdundubhi; pralaya-abhra-rava + upamam → pralayābhraravopamam; daityaiḥ + mahā-vyomni → daityairmahāvyomni; tala + utthitaiḥ → talotthitaiḥ.

words.gloss: comparable to the roar of a dissolution-cloud
risen from the floor of the underworld

units.speaker: narrator
units.devanagari:
कालक्षेपकरं घोरं पुनर्युद्धमवर्तत |
पुनः पलायनं चक्रुरयुध्यन्त पुनः सुराः ||
units.iast:
kālakṣepakaraṃ ghoraṃ punaryuddhamavartata |
punaḥ palāyanaṃ cakrurayudhyanta punaḥ surāḥ ||
units.english: {2:Again} {3:a war}, {1:dreadful}, {0:causing time to pass}, {4:occurred}. {5:Again} {10:the gods} {6,7:took flight}; {9:again} {8:they fought}.
units.sense: Again a war, dreadful, causing time to pass, occurred. Again the gods took flight; again they fought.

grammar.karakaSummary: kāla-kṣepa-karam and ghoram qualify yuddham, the subject of avartata; surāḥ is kartṛ of cakruḥ and ayudhyanta; palāyanam is karman of cakruḥ.
grammar.verbalModality: avartata and ayudhyanta are imperfect middle; cakruḥ is perfect third plural. The three occurrences of punaḥ respectively qualify the renewed war, the flight, and the renewed fighting.
grammar.sandhi: punar + yuddham → punaryuddham; yuddham + avartata → yuddhamavartata; cakruḥ + ayudhyanta → cakrurayudhyanta; the following punaḥ and surāḥ remain separately articulated.

units.speaker: narrator
units.devanagari:
एवं ते कालहरणं युद्धेन सुरपुङ्गवाः |
चक्रुर्नानाविधोपायैर्दैत्यव्यामोहकारणात् ||
units.iast:
evaṃ te kālaharaṇaṃ yuddhena surapuṅgavāḥ |
cakrurnānāvidhopāyairdaityavyāmohakāraṇāt ||
units.english: {0:Thus} {1:those} {4:bulls among the gods} {5:effected} {2:the taking-away of time} {3:through battle}, {6:by various kinds of expedients}, {7:for causing bewilderment among the demons}.
units.sense: Thus those bulls among the gods effected the taking-away of time through battle, by various kinds of expedients, for causing bewilderment among the demons.

grammar.karakaSummary: te sura-puṅgavāḥ is kartṛ; kāla-haraṇam is karman; yuddhena and nānā-vidhopāyaiḥ are instrumental means; daitya-vyāmoha-kāraṇāt is an ablative of motive/cause.
grammar.sandhi: cakruḥ + nānā → cakrurnānā; vidha + upāyaiḥ → vidhopāyaiḥ; upāyaiḥ + daitya → upāyairdaitya.

words.gloss: for/on account of causing bewilderment among demons

units.speaker: narrator
units.devanagari:
एतावता च कालेन दृढाभ्यासादहंकृतेः |
दामादयोऽहमित्यास्थां जगृहुर्युक्तचेतसः ||
units.iast:
etāvatā ca kālena dṛḍhābhyāsādahaṃkṛteḥ |
dāmādayo'hamityāsthāṃ jagṛhuryuktacetasaḥ ||
units.english: {1:And} {0:over this much} {2:time}, {3:from firm repetition} {4:of I-making}, {5:Dāma and the others}, {10:their minds yoked}, {9:took up} {8:the attachment} {6:'I'} {7:as such}.
units.sense: And over this much time, from firm repetition of I-making, Dāma and the others, their minds yoked, took up the attachment 'I' as such.

grammar.karakaSummary: dāmādayaḥ/yukta-cetasaḥ is kartṛ; āsthām is karman of jagṛhuḥ; aham iti specifies its content; etāvatā kālena is instrumental extent; dṛḍha-abhyāsāt is causal ablative governing ahaṃ-kṛteḥ as genitive.
grammar.verbalModality: jagṛhuḥ is perfect third plural; yukta is a completed-action participle within a bahuvrīhi.
grammar.sandhi: abhyāsāt + ahaṃ-kṛteḥ → abhyāsādahaṃkṛteḥ; dāma-ādayaḥ + aham + iti + āsthām → dāmādayo'hamityāsthām; jagṛhuḥ + yukta → jagṛhuryukta.

words.karaka: karaṇa/extent over which the change occurred

words.note: Kāśikā defines abhyāsa as repeated doing/recurrence.
The form is the action noun 'I-making' (ahaṃ-kṛti), from aham + √kṛ + ktin.

alternatives.qualification: Dhātupāṭha separately transmits the samādhi root; context permits this alongside the joining/yoking root
